claims.value: A naïve CD4-positive T cell binds antigen-presenting cells through their antigen-loaded MHC II molecules and is stimulated to become a helper T cell, which then stimulates B cells or cytotoxic T cells directly or secretes cytokines that alert other cells to the pathogen.
claims.quote: Naïve CD4+ cells bind APCs via their antigen-embedded MHC II molecules and are stimulated to become helper T (TH) lymphocytes, cells that go on to stimulate B cells (or cytotoxic T cells) directly or secrete cytokines to inform more and various target cells about the pathogenic threat.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Its CD4 marker works as a cell adhesion molecule, binding the MHC molecule on an antigen-presenting cell to keep the T cell in close contact with that cell.
claims.quote: These markers are cell adhesion molecules that keep the T cell in close contact with the antigen-presenting cell by directly binding to the MHC molecule (to a different part of the molecule than does the antigen).
